title: Two paper rotors in series: two different hidden wirings (form H, mostly cannot be judged) and one hidden strip used there and back (form B, dead)
k4_result: 598,807,128 settings. Form H (two different hidden wirings, 229.8M settings): 0 settings reach the 5 closed loops needed to count; the most any surviving setting has is 3 (11 settings). Form B (second rotor = the first read backwards, 369.0M settings): 31 settings pass the loop test, 20 of them with 2 or more loops; for all 20 the pieces of wiring do not fit on one strip, so 0 are left and there is nothing to read.
controls: 3 shuffled K4s (small families and shorter keys in full, a different third of the words and of the longest keys each, about 218.9M settings each). Form H: 0 settings with 5 loops, best 3 loops in all three (7, 5 and 26 word settings with 3 loops). Form B: 6, 10 and 0 survivors with 2 or more loops; 0 fit on one strip. Same picture as K4.
planted: 6/6 (form H: word key, 3-letter key, constant speed with a stepping slow rotor; form B: the same three, and the planted message is read back, 67-85 of 97 letters, English score -4.2 to -4.8). The form H messages were redrawn until the true setting had 5 loops (draws 11, 6 and 2395): that is the limit of form H, not a trick.
scope_limits: Form H is NOT ruled out. 24 clue letters against two hidden wirings (52 contacts) force too little: only 1.5% of true word-key settings, 14.3% of true 3-letter-key settings and 0.0% of true constant-speed settings make the 5 loops needed, so 86-100% of form H could be true and invisible. Form B is covered for: fast turn = 26 constant speeds, previous cipher letter, running sum of the cipher text, 248,495 dictionary words of 2-22 letters (plain, running sum, or +1 per letter; A-Z or KRYPTOS numbering), every key of length 1-4; slow turn = constant inside each clue block with block 2 d = 0-25 further on, one step per pass of the key, and for the small families a step every 2-12 letters or a second constant speed. Limits inside form B: for words the slow strip's start is 0-25 only with d = 0, and start 0 only with d = 1-25; keys of length 4 and all words only with both rotors turning the same way; keys longer than 4 only if they are dictionary words. Not covered at all: one strip used twice in the same direction (R2 = R1), slow rotor stepping inside a clue block for word keys, three rotors, a reflector.

negative.family: Two paper rotors in series with hidden wirings
negative.hypothesis: K4 is two rotors in series, C = R2[R1[P+s]-s+t]-t, fast turn s from a speed, word or short key, slow turn t constant inside each clue block (or stepping rarely); either both wirings hidden and different (form H) or the second rotor is the first one read backwards (form B).
negative.scope: 598.8M settings by an exact loop test on the contact graph (no wiring guessed). Fast turn: 26 speeds, 2 cipher-fed rules, 248,495 words x 3 schemes x 2 numberings, every key of length 1-5 (H) / 1-4 (B). Slow turn: block 2 shifted by 0-25, one step per key pass, rare steps. A-Z/KRYPTOS faces. Form B survivors must also fit on one strip and read as English.
negative.outcome: Form B dead in scope: 20 K4 settings pass the loop test with 2+ loops, 0 fit on one strip (3 shuffled K4s: 6, 10, 0 pass, 0 fit); 98.6-99.6% of true settings would be caught; planted 3/3 read back. Form H: no signal but mostly undecidable: K4 0 settings with 5+ loops, best 3 (shuffled: 0, best 3); only 0-14% of true settings can reach 5 loops; planted 3/3 among those. Two different hidden wirings stay open.

follow_ups: One hidden strip used twice in the same direction (R2 = R1, C = R[R[P+s]-s+t]-t). 26 unknown contacts against 24 clue letters, about 5 letters over-determined, so it is decidable, but the equations are not linear: it needs a backtracking search over the wiring per setting (start with the small families: speeds, short keys).

Two rotors where one wiring is a dictionary keyword alphabet and only the other is hidden: with R2 known the test becomes idea 72's wire-collision test on Y = R2back[C+t]-t, with about 8 forced coincidences, so every word key is decidable. Cost: 220k alphabets x fast rules; needs a hash join or a small fast-rule set.

Form H can only be decided with more plaintext: each extra known letter adds one edge to the contact graph, and only closed loops of edges test anything. Re-run attacks/82 unchanged if another clue or K5 gives more letters under the same key.
